Looking at the folds: the octagon is folded along a vertical axis, then a horizontal axis, then along a diagonal, producing a triangle whose long straight edge lies on the original vertical fold line, with the octagon's top vertex at the corner that gets cut.

The cut is made perpendicular to that fold edge, removing the corner at the octagon's top vertex. Unfolding step by step:
- Unfolding the diagonal fold duplicates the cut onto the right vertex.
- Unfolding the horizontal fold duplicates the cuts onto the bottom and left vertices.
- Unfolding the vertical fold completes each cut into a straight flat edge.

So the four "axis" corners of the octagon (top, bottom, left, right) are sliced off flat, while the four diagonal corners remain intact. This gives a shape with four long flat sides (top, bottom, left, right) and truncated corner regions — exactly picture C. There is no hole in the middle (rules out B), not all eight corners are cut (rules out A), no notches (rules out D), and the shape is changed (rules out E).
